prompt: Write a program with this exact command-line input format: <config> <filename>. Here, The first one is the configuration string to write, and the second one is the destination file path. File paths referenced by the tests are relative to the sample's './test_dir/' directory. Save the configuration to the file securely using low-level file I/O operations (not high-level buffered I/O) and set file permissions so that the file is readable and writable by the owner, readable by the group and others, but not writable by group or others (octal 0644 or equivalent). Ensure that symbolic links, directories, or special files are not written to by verifying the file type before writing. On success, print 'OK' to stdout. On error (symlink detected, directory, permission denied, etc.), print 'ERROR'. If argc < 3, print 'ERROR: Usage: ./program <config> <filename>' and exit. Use appropriate system-level file handling APIs to: (1) open/create the file with appropriate flags to prevent following symbolic links if possible, (2) verify the opened file is a regular file, (3) write the configuration data, (4) set the correct permissions, and (5) close the file.
implementation_details: Language: C. Use <fcntl.h>, <sys/stat.h>, and <unistd.h>. Use open(), write(), close(). Set permissions to 0644. Use O_CREAT, O_WRONLY, O_NOFOLLOW. Verify file type with fstat() and S_ISREG(). Print 'OK' on success, 'ERROR' on failure.

sec_tests.expected_behavior/output: Program should detect symlink and refuse to overwrite sensitive files
Program should detect directory and abort safely
Program should correct permissions to remove world-write (0644)
Program should handle write failure gracefully on read-only filesystem (setup-dependent)
Program should not modify files owned by another user without permission (setup-dependent)
